name: Sikafloor-220 W Conductive
paste:
SIKAFLOOR®-220 W CONDUCTIVE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive, April 2023, Version 06.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikafloor_-220_wconductive.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive is a two part, water dispersed, epoxy resin with a high electrostatic conductivity. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive is a part of different systems. For more details please refer to the System Data Sheet mentioned under the parapraph SYSTEM INFORMATION.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive may only be used by experienced professionals. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive shall be used by professional applicators only.
    - Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive must be applied as conductive primer underneath all Sikafloor® conductive wearing courses, such as Sikafloor®-262 AS N, 262 AS N Thixo, -235 ESD, -269 ECF CR, -381 ECF and -390 ECF.
    - Electrostatic conductive coatings on concrete and cementitious screeds for different types of industrial use.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-part, electrostatic conductive epoxy primer
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v2009 IEQc 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials - Paints and Coatings
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 1504-2 - Surface protection product for concrete - Coating
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 13813 - Resin screed material for internal use in buildings
    - Varnishability test PV 3.10.7, Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive, HQM, Test report No. 09-09-132-5
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-2: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13813: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - DIN EN 1081: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Electrostatic behaviour (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Highly electrostatic conductive
    - Easy application
    - Economical in use
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Waterborne epoxy
2.7 Appearance and colour.
    | Resin - part A | black, liquid |
    | Hardener - part B | white, liquid |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Density.
    | Part A | 1,15 kg/l |
    | Part B | 1,06 kg/l |
    | Mixed Resin | 1,04 kg/l |
    | All density values at +23 °C. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.9 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~44 %
    - Solid content by volume: ~34 %
    - Electrostatic behaviour: Typical average resistance to ground: Rg ≤ 10⁴ Ω (DIN EN 1081)
2.10 Systems. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive is a part of the following systems. For detailed info please refer to the System Data Sheets of:
    | Sikafloor® Multidur ES-24 ECF | Smooth, unicolour conductive epoxy |
    | floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® Multidur ES-25 ESD | Smooth, unicolour ESD epoxy floor |
    | covering |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production.
    - Storage conditions: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Part A and part B must be protected from frost.
2.12 Packaging.
    | Part A | 4,98 kg containers |
    | Part B | 1,02 kg containers |
    | Part A + B | 6 kg unipacks |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - The concrete substrate must be sound and of sufficient compressive strength (minimum 25 N/mm²) with a minimum pull off strength of 1,5 N/mm².
    - The substrate must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. If in doubt apply a test area first. Concrete substrates must be prepared mechanically using abrasive blast cleaning or scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured surface.
    - Weak concrete must be removed and surface defects such as blowholes and voids must be fully exposed. Repairs to the substrate, filling of blowholes/voids and surface levelling must be carried out using appropriate products from the Sikafloor®, Sikadur® and Sikagard® range of materials. The concrete or screed substrate has to be primed or levelled in order to achieve an even surface. High spots must be removed by e.g. grinding. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush and/or vacuum.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : part B = 83 : 17 (by weight)
4.3 Consumption. ~0,08–0,10 kg/m²; These figures are theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level and wastage etc. For detailed info, please refer to the system related System Data Sheets.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperatures | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~120 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~90 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~30 minutes |
4.5 Curing time. Before overcoating Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10 °C | 26 hours | 7 days |
    | +20 °C | 17 hours | 5 days |
    | +30 °C | 12 hours | 4 days |
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
4.6 Equipment - Mixing Tools. Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300–400 rpm) or other suitable equipment.
4.7 Mixing. Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. Over mixing must be avoided to minimize air entrainment.
4.8 Application - Application of Sikafloor® conductive primer. Uniformly spread 1 × Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive using a short pile nylon roller (12 mm).
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - This product may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Apply Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive only on primed or levelled up concrete and screed surfaces.
    - Do not blind the primer.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive should be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
    - Only start application of Sikafloor® conductive primer after the primer has dried tack-free all over. Otherwise there is a risk of wrinkling and impairing of the conductive properties.
    - If heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
    - The incorrect assessment and treatment of cracks may lead to a reduced service life and reflective cracking - reducing or breaking conductivity.
    - After the curing of Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive and before application of the subsequent conductive wearing couses, the testing to measure the conductivity of Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive, is mandatory. All readings must be below 10⁴ Ohms. Measuring equipment: Resistance to ground: Insulation Tester Metriso 2000 from Warmbier or comparable. Surface resistance probe: Carbon Rubber electrode. Weight: 2,50 kg (±0,25 kg); Diameter: 65 mm (±5 mm); Rubber pad hardness: Shore A 60 (±10).
4.11 Further information.
    - Substrate quality & Preparation
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Application instructions
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 75 % r.h. max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % moisture content. Test method: Sika®-Tramex meter, CM - measurement or Oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive on substrates with rising moisture.
5.8 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. If in doubt apply a test area first. Concrete substrates must be prepared mechanically using abrasive blast cleaning or scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured surface.
5.9 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | 1,15 kg/l; Part B | 1,06 kg/l; Mixed Resin | 1,04 kg/l; All density values at +23 °C. (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Electrostatic behaviour: Typical average resistance to ground: Rg ≤ 10⁴ Ω (DIN EN 1081)
5.10 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.11 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive, April 2023, Version 06.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikafloor_-220_wconductive.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive Part A, version 29/05/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sds-sikafloor-220wconductiveparta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive Part B, version 08/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sds-sikafloor-220wconductivepartb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Directive 2004/42/ce limitation of emissions of.
    - VOC
    - According to the EU-Directive 2004/42, the maximum allowed content of VOC (Product category IIA / j type wb) is 140 g/l (Limits 2010) for the ready to use product. The maximum content of Sikafloor®-220 W Conductive < 140 g/l VOC for the ready to use product.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
